ranking_policy: Multi-agent coordination scan for mini-ork, a task OS that runs many concurrent coding agents (recipe DAG nodes, goal-loops, shell-launched RSI loops, interactive Claude/codex sessions) against shared repositories, shared config, and a shared state database. The problem: independent agents silently overlap — editing the same files or settings, working the same topic twice, or messaging short-lived workers — and nothing detects it after start-up. Rank 2026 papers by how directly their technique detects, prevents, or resolves overlap/conflict between concurrent agents at runtime (per turn or per action): concurrency control, intent/claim publication, shared workspaces and blackboards, conflict-aware memory, coordination protocols, runtime monitoring, and semantic merge conflict detection rank highest; papers matched by multiple topics rank above single-topic matches; break ties by citation signal and recency.
